interactions.title: Riswynn’s purpose and the quieted crown
lines: Riswynn: She goes to, you know, talk to Kethra, but mainly she wants to start bouncing ideas off of Nuzkar and Aygul. Okay, cool, to begin the process. Begin a discourse with the orcs about a strategy, for what are their key hopes for progress?
Kenzo: Is Riswynn wearing the crown like right now? Are you like wearing it? You're just like—where do you keep it?

Riswynn: Well given that the return to Vindristjarna is also the beginning of the recruitment for the war against Thark, she figured that she would wear it, and and approach Kethra and the rainbow orcs with this with this newfound clarity, and say—

Riswynn: You know we're aware of the power of this artifact, and the way that I've chosen to harness its good for the world is to address Thark's evil influence and make some changes in a larger population of Orcs, and see what we can do. But what should be our goals?
Kenzo: Can I soul sight Riswynn when she's wearing a crown?
DM: I mean she's still Riswynn.
Kenzo: But like, you know, Riswynn, plus like what's what's going on?

DM: So I mean, it's it's like there's none of the weird energy that used to be coming off of it right? There's none of the like tendrils of all of the people trapped in your mirror, who were possessed by the cleansed, are presumably now just standing around confused about what's going on.
Riswynn: Good reminder. We should talk to them.
DM: There's no—so I mean, that's— But otherwise she's yeah. I mean, like, I think, like Kate said, right? She's like pretty—

DM: The crown is much more like at peace than it was before. Right? Like it's more—it's not Riswynn fighting to shift the crown into some other kind of form. It's like the crown and Riswynn are one, you know, not exactly one entity, but, like, you know, clearly— connected in a way, or united in a single purpose, I guess, is the better way to put it.

before: Wellby: The armor itself is is this wide leather belt tooled with Kenku designs around his waist, and he's—

Wellby: I don't know. There's just an ease there like, I think, for so long. You know so much of his routine always was like, Be prepared! What's coming next, and what's around the corner? And he's not missing anything. But—but there's there's just an ease to it like there's not for the 1st time in so so long there's not something hanging over.

Wellby: Meanwhile Baxter is is out of the stable and down on the ground, running around, chasing after lizards and trying to catch a rabbit that's just a little bit too quick for him. Yeah. Wellby's sitting back with his feet up, and maybe idly arguing with Kenzo over Chardon things, not out of any real conviction, but out of, you know the long habit about disagreeing over, Chardon.

Riswynn: Riswynn is, you know, still armored. Still, you know, post the time in the darkness and the time in the great halls, sort of coming down off of the intense ending of the changing into animals and chasing all around the—for to find the Prismwell.

Riswynn: But it didn't take like a huge physical toll. She still looks neat, and, you know, ready to fight. But what's most different for her is that she's not distracted by sort of trying to pay attention to the crisis of the moment, and also wrestle with what's on her head. And what she's able to do now is think: there will be planning, there will be focus. There will be a purposeful mission, and, and feel some sort of hope and direction. And instead of, how can I fix this? How can I wrestle this into situation that can be rescued? Now there's a—now there's a clarity.
after: Kenzo: Alright. So we're not like preparing to roll initiative, but we're all we're all happy and—
DM: You know I mean, Riswynn would probably like thrash you all, anyway, now that she has 9th level spells.
Kenzo: Oh, boy!
Delwath: Doesn't Seeker also have 9th level spells?
DM: That's true. Seeker also has ninth.

interactions.title: Sura’s news from Dunmar
lines: Kenzo: All right, let's—Kenzo pulls out the sending stone, and dials Sura's number.
DM: So you get Sura as she— Yes.

Kenzo: Sura, it's it's Kenzo. We are back on this plane after after being gone for a little bit, but just calling to hear—wanted to see how things are going with you, and how how things are playing out in Dunmar, and if you had any engagement with Chardon or any Chardon related entities recently?
DM: I, so much has happened. I don't remember the last news you had. I think you've been gone a while. Yes.
Kenzo: Yeah. What? What's been? What's been happening the last 3, 3 or 4 weeks last month?
DM: Well, let's see last—did I tell you? Did we speak after the slip—surrender of the legions?
DM: Yes, we spoke then. I remember that clearly. Since then—

DM: Wow, that I wouldn't say it's been exactly quiet. But after a general Cusico, so Marius Cusico, he turned and headed back to Chardon. It was the strangest thing just said, “This is a pointless fight,” and surrendered. I think you had something to do with that, didn't you?
DM: Things were confused at that moment.
Kenzo: Yeah, you could say, certain people were released from a certain type of bondage they were experiencing before.
DM: So he took the bulk of his legions and started marching back to Chardon.
DM: I don't know. We didn't follow him that far.
DM: Once they crossed back across the Myraeni Gap and started heading along the Chardon-Tokra Road, not my concern.
DM: Bigger problem was the disgruntled looters who refused to march with Cusico and claimed they had come for booty, and, "We're gonna get booty."
DM: Sort of annoyed. He didn't do anything about it, but maybe he was more worried about the 7th Legion, the mage folks who snuck off in the night towards the north.
DM: I don't know. I think there's something going on in Chardon; I haven't been able to get clear reports, which is strange. But—
DM: Yeah, he left. We were left to deal with the looters. Let's see.

DM: There was only maybe 5, 6 days ago. They attacked parts parts of Songara, but Havdar engaged them, scattered them into the Myraeni Gap. I suspect there will be bandit trouble for some time, but nothing we can't handle.
DM: Shadow assassins in Tokra were a bit more of a problem. But was it you, again, who contacted the stoneborn?
Delwath: Yeah, didn't we do that? Yeah, we did.
Kenzo: What happened? I remember. What did we do?
Delwath: We sent a message to Drikod's village.
Delwath: To have the Stoneborn try and help with the chaos.
DM: Well, they turned out to be very helpful—the second time in as many centuries they've saved Tokra, so we're grateful for that. And honestly, things are a lot less bad than they could have been.
Kenzo: How are things with your brother?
DM: I mean nothing there has gone the way it should have. I don't know. I I do not understand him anymore, and can't get in his head.
Kenzo: You think he was under the influence, or has been, or was, or continues to be, influenced by anyone or anything? Or is this just his own evolution over time?
Kenzo: The crown wasn't controlling him, was he?
DM: Was it? I don't think so. I think just everything made him paranoid and cautious, and cautious and paranoid is a difficult combination, to lead from.
DM: I mean, there was no chance he was going to fight the Chardonian navy, so I'm not surprised, he surrendered. Darba—can't see a future where we are—
DM: I can't see a future where Tokra and Songara and the Eastern deserts submit to his leadership again, not after everything.
Kenzo: And where is he now?
DM: Oh, I guess, in Darba or Nayahar, probably still negotiating the terms of his surrender to the Chardonian Emperor.
Kenzo: When you say something weird is happening in Chardon, what do you mean?

DM: The legions just suddenly surrendered and turned and marched away. And and, I've not had any news formally ending a state of conflict between us. I've not heard any information about whether you are still enemies of the State to be executed on sight.
DM: I have not heard any response to the—there's been no peace—
Kenzo: When you communicate in this whole process of these past months, when you communicate with any Chardonian entity, who are you communicating with?
DM: I mean it's all by courier and pigeon.
Kenzo: You know who you're communicating with them?
DM: I know the seals of the Emperor. But who's to say if those are faked or not?
Kenzo: Is it is, but is it through the Emperor?
DM: Well, the magistros, as he calls himself. But yes, the Emperor.
Kenzo: What was your last communication?
DM: It must have been of—I think it must have been.

DM: Almost to more than a month ago now, when the Chardonians accused you of terrorism and Dunmar, of harboring fugitives, and demanded that we hand you over and pay a blood price for the damage done to the city or war would be declared.
DM: I know that he was in Darba 4 weeks ago, when the Chardonian navy captured the city. I don't know if he's still in Darba. I—
DM: Karnas does not see fit to keep me in his council, with these looters on our border. It's not been easy to focus on gathering news elsewhere.
DM: And, of course, as you know, I'm much prefer to be riding at the front of an army than sitting behind a desk.
Kenzo: Politics is unfortunately a part of your future now. But—
Kenzo: But this has been helpful. Thank you for—thank you for sharing the updates, and glad that things are in a greater state of calm now.
DM: How goes you? I—you've been unreachable for weeks?
Kenzo: Yeah, we had to go to another dimension and deal with some fey related misadventures. But we're fine. Everything everything is well.
DM: That's good to hear. Fey are tricky.
Kenzo: Oh, we know. Oh, we know. Tricky is the right adjective.
Kenzo: But hopefully we'll we'll be able to come, visit and see see you in Tokra before before long—on, yeah.
DM: Just returned here from riding the border. Havdar is still organizing some war bands to deal with bandits.
DM: But until there's peace there won't—formal peace, anyway, it's not like there's going to be trade with Chardon to begin with. So.
Kenzo: Do you have any contacts in Chardon, anyone, close or official, otherwise, that we might be able to contact?
DM: I mean you remember, I've only been—
Kenzo: Yeah, I was just asking.
DM: Sort of laughs. No, I have not been to Chardon.
Kenzo: Just figured during this whole period of turbulence, if you were interacting with anyone. But if not, that's fine.

before: Delwath: Yeah.
Kenzo: Servius! Again.
DM: Servius was the guy who was like a historian with the open scroll, who—
Delwath: Right.

DM: Passed through— Karawa like shortly before the campaign started, and then was always seemed like he was one step ahead of you tracking artifacts, and you followed him to Darba because you thought he had the cloak or something. You weren't sure what, but it turned out to be a red herring. And then he went off into Illoria somewhere, and you, almost like went to go, do some adventure, and then decided not to in a rare display of focus.
after: Wellby: That's tricky.
DM: The messenger symmetry—sorry. Go ahead!
Wellby: I'm sorry. It just strikes me as a funny symmetry that we were just in the Feywild freeing a queen who had been trapped in an extra dimensional prison for an indeterminate amount of time.
Delwath: Hmm.
DM: You do have a bit, you are! She laughs, and she sort of laughs. Delwath, is she gonna join our support group?

interactions.title: Sura asks about Agata’s prison
lines: Wellby: I'm sorry. It just strikes me as a funny symmetry that we were just in the Feywild freeing a queen who had been trapped in an extra dimensional prison for an indeterminate amount of time.
DM: You do have a bit, you are! She laughs, and she sort of laughs. Delwath, is she gonna join our support group?
Delwath: I think she's a different—
Wellby: She moves in different circles.
Delwath: Her entrapment, I think, was of a different nature, and she, I think, is of a different nature. Add—
Delwath: And and she is not an ordinary fey, at—she is probably one of the few original fey still alive.
DM: By any chance, while you were passing through the Feywild happened to check to make sure that Agata is still imprisoned?
Kenzo: I'm sure that's fine. That whole situation.
Delwath: But wait, hold on! We had a way of sending a message to Cloudspinner, right?
Wellby: Well. Wellby puts his hand over the phone for just a sec. She's definitely escaped by now, right?
Kenzo: I'm sure she's totally not in captivity.
Delwath: She hasn't just— There's no [garbled]—
Kenzo: I'm sure it's I'm sure that situation is totally under control.
((Reminder of the hat’s ordinary travel function))
Delwath: I mean, maybe we should ask Cloudspinner to check up on her. She, Agata, did betray Cloudspinner's allies, right?
Delwath: So I mean, you know, we might just wanna inform the Cloudspinner of Agata's fate, and just ask her to make sure that you know she stays where she belongs.
Delwath: That might have been a good thing to remind her of when we were there, but we had other problems.
DM: Anything else I can tell you? Now, what are you doing next?

Kenzo: We're still deciding. We'll we'll let you know how things unfold. But you can reach us, obviously at any time. But we'll we'll let you know—we. We may investigate things a little bit further in Chardon. But there's some loose ends to tie up there, but—
DM: You know you'd be welcome anytime you wish to visit Tokra.
Kenzo: We definitely will be back to Tokra sooner than than later. My my staff misses Tokra, for sure. Thank you. Thank you, Sura. Hmm!

before: Kenzo: Yeah, I was just asking.
DM: Sort of laughs. No, I have not been to Chardon.
Kenzo: Just figured during this whole period of turbulence, if you were interacting with anyone. But if not, that's fine.
Wellby: That's tricky.
DM: The messenger symmetry—sorry. Go ahead!
after: Kenzo: Do we? How do we contact people far away other than sending stones?
DM: Dreams, Delwath.
Delwath: You can cast dream which lets us lets anybody talk to somebody, but they have to be asleep.
DM: And Riswynn can cast—well, maybe doesn't have sending prepared so that doesn't help you. But—
Delwath: In general can cast, sending.

interactions.title: Avaras watches Kenzo’s mastery
lines: DM: So so as you do this, you see, like Avaras over in the corner, kind of watching you with a smile on his face, one of the only remaining masters of the Order of the Awakened Soul.
DM: But even he has not progressed to this level of connection with the with this sort of spirit realm and the plane of consciousness, and just kind of—

DM: You know, he was never really your teacher much, but, like he—he was the one who originally taught you stunning strikes like a year ago. And of course helped like get you connected and grounded after you went through the whole Bhishma initiation thing, and there's clearly like a sort of look of of pride in his eyes as he's sort of smiling, watching across the the desert, not interrupting the moment exactly, but just kind of, you know, aware and and watching.

before: Kenzo: Yeah, that's like Kenzo, and Wellby like, are just kind of like shadow boxing like Kenzo's like trying to like figure out like, "I'm solid. I'm not solid." I'm solid. I'm not solid."
Wellby: Wellby rapidly escalates to seeing if he can actually hit you.
Kenzo: Yeah. Kenzo rapidly escalates into like trying to like, you know, dodge, and hit.
DM: Yeah, I mean, he's not any harder to hit than he usually is, which is pretty hard. But—
DM: So as you—so a couple of things. One is—
after: DM: So as you settle down to a dinner, a raucous dinner with everybody, Riswynn and the Orcs, and everybody sort of talking about what's next, and a sort of general mood of just relaxation sort of spreading across the group, as many of the people you've traveled with have really only ever experienced their lives as chasing you from crisis to crisis. And now it sort of seems like, maybe they, you know, this, at least, is a moment where that doesn't feel like it's happening.

DM: Amil, as Amil, as is his wont, is always cheerful and happy, and just like trying everything that Delwath made and like complimenting the food, and you know, dragging everybody off their feet to dance.
DM: Égnir, the elf, is normally quite quiet and sort of meditative and sort of stays in the background, just focused more on plants than people. Comes out of the shell a little bit.
DM: Mica Copperharp, one of the halflings is a great musician, and, you know, takes up— whatever he plays, I don't know what it is. I'll make up something. Faldrak, of course, you know it's Faldrak.

DM: He has not experienced his life as chasing you from crisis to crisis. He's experienced it as a rousing adventure, full of interesting situations, has taken the lesson that the right thing to do in any situation is to run towards whatever seems most interesting.

Kenzo: Alright!

interactions.title: Xavier’s dream: riots, Andros and a safe return
lines: DM: So as you fall into sleep, what? What is—you can control the appearance of the dream.
Kenzo: Yeah. So we—in the dream, the dream setting.

Kenzo: It'll be this little, this square in Chardon, where, when we were little kids like, you know, Kenzo and Xavier would go like run around and like in the marketplace, because they would go like steal food and stuff like that. And so there's like a particular stand that they would go to that had this, you know, kind of local Chardonian like set of sweets that they would like, go and steal stuff, and so they would often go there, steal this treat, and go to this alley around the corner and go eat it. And so in the dream, Kenzo kind of appears like with Xavier, like sitting in that alley where they used to sit when they were little kids, like eating there, eating the little, you know candies, or whatever that they stole from the market around the corner.
DM: So as you appear in the dream, Xavier is sitting next to you. He is—doesn't look too changed, actually.
DM: Except he's got a fresh like broke—like broken nose, and like a like a big bruise across, like half of his face.
Kenzo: Fresh like a fresh wound? Or is it like actually—
DM: Yeah, like a fresh wound like a few few days ago, maybe a week ago. It's like, clearly, still healing.
DM: And he's sitting and like eating sweets and just smiles and laughs to himself.
DM: Now, what made me dream of this?
Kenzo: And then Kenzo looks at him, and he's like—
Kenzo: Pretty good, right? Almost as good as you remember?
DM: Kind of starts and looks over.
DM: Yeah, sure. Isn't this me remembering?

Kenzo: Oh, and Kenzo is dressed like himself, so he looks like like, you know, 5 years ago he was like looking like whatever, and now he's like in a like—looks like a monk like, like you just interviewed somebody that could like, you know, fuck somebody up and has his has a staff and stuff like that. And it's just like, you know.
DM: Is this some wish fulfillment? Could use a brawler.
DM: I said, is this some wish fulfillment? I could use a brawler.
Kenzo: I don't know. Maybe your dreams are about to come true. How are you, man?
Kenzo: By the way, you're dreaming right now. But we're actually having this conversation, just so, you know. "It's me." That starts slightly.
Kenzo: What happened to your face? Not cognizant of it.
DM: Got got caught in one of the brawls of about a week ago.
Kenzo: I mean, you normally are kind of ugly, but this is worse than normal.
DM: It's been crazy, man, you know the Eightfold Flame?
Kenzo: Yeah. Well, what's—tell me more about them. I've heard a little bit. What's going on with the Eightfold Flame?
DM: It was the strangest thing, maybe 3 weeks ago, something like that.

DM: A bunch of bureaucrats in the chalyte trade published manifesto, Break the Stone, accusing the merchants in the Hetaeri Magica, who control the trade, of all sorts of things like they knew how dangerous it was, and they didn't care, and it was—
DM: I don't know what happened there, man, I mean.
DM: I would have never—I thought those people like money, right? I mean—
DM: Can't imagine any of them kept their jobs after that.
Kenzo: Wait. Sorry! Who's he saying publish something?
Delwath: The chalyte direct—the the bureaucrats in the chalyte factory, isn't all—isn't this the people you made do this?
Kenzo: Oh! Oh! This is me doing that.
Kenzo: When I, when I briefly had the crown.
Kenzo: Nice, nice, nice, okay. Laughs when he hears about this. Yeah. So they published an expose on themselves.
Kenzo: Kenzo, when Xavier's like—Kenzo starts laughing hysterically. Okay. Oh, oh, I didn't know about that. But that's pretty funny.
DM: I mean you laugh. But, man, it got out of control fast. Pretty soon they were you know, preaching about—
DM: And you know any true believer in the in Mos Numena must reject the corrupting influence of chalyte, even—
Kenzo: Okay, okay. That's when the whole Eightfold Flame—
DM: Burning purity of holy fire.

DM: But, hey, man, I mean, never in my life have I seen people rising up against you know the merchants Guild and the chalyte processors guild and—and you know I'm not one to shy from a fight. So hey, I started punching, too.
Kenzo: And that was a week ago. What's going on now?
DM: For a minute there we managed to control the whole north bank of the Chasa more or less.
DM: I mean, the factories are all beaten to shreds now. Nobody could stop that. Fires broke out, pretty toxic there for a little bit since—
DM: Since the magistros returned a few days ago, and blockaded the bridges and imposed a curfew. Things have been a bit tough.
DM: I don't know, man. Yesterday he issued the Imperial order.

DM: I don't know. That's all above me a little bit, something about improving safety in the chalyte processing and introducing some imperial licensure required for operating a mill and basically stripping it from everybody who owned one. But I don't know. Didn't seem like it was good enough to me.
Kenzo: Wait. So the Emperor is trying to take back control over the chalyte trade, now that they're trying to stomp out the—
DM: So that's all above my pay grade. I—
Kenzo: I guess I'm saying, is he? He's cracking down, whereas—
DM: I mean, that's what it sounded like. But the the leaders tell us it's not enough.
Kenzo: Oh, they're saying the concessions are not enough?
Delwath: Riswynn's crown energy is now all directed to the Orcs, right?
Delwath: Riswynn, yeah, where's your crown brain going?
DM: It's not the—these people are not, yeah, not even connected that. Yeah.
Riswynn: So, whatever they were doing—
Kenzo: Oh, this is what's on its own thing.
Delwath: It's now going on its own. It's not the crown. Yeah.
Kenzo: Yeah, so so just and last thing, Xavier, thank you. This has been very helpful, and and I hope to see you soon. By the way I know this is all a little strange.
DM: You're you're not near here, are you?
Kenzo: No, no, but I have the—one of my companions has the magic ability to teleport, so I might. I might show up sooner than later. But anyways ignore that, for now. You're sleeping.
DM: You are a—yeah, nobody. The magistros has not rescinded the declaration describing you as an enemy of the State.
Kenzo: Oh, so I'm still an enemy of the State?
Wellby: Still work to your advantage.
DM: I I don't know what to tell you, man. I—when when rumors were going around that you destroyed the Kylos Market with a portal to Pandemonium, I was a bit surprised.
Kenzo: Oh, that wasn't me. Yeah, just so, you know, that totally wasn't me.
DM: Yeah, there was other rumors that it was all a scam, but I mean, believe those—that this is—
DM: You always had it out for this city. I was like, "Go, go, Ken!" I mean, I wouldn't have picked that exact form of revenge, but like—
Kenzo: No, no, no, that's not my style. That's not my style. Yeah, I haven't changed that much. Yeah, look, so, okay. So this is the situation. Who are the leaders of the Eightfold Flame?
DM: That's above my pay grade.
Kenzo: You think you can figure it out?
DM: I'm just a bruiser here.
((Table suggestion to ask for Xavier’s contact))
Kenzo: Yeah. Well, he's not in the Eightfold Flame. This guy.
Kenzo: No, I don't think so.
Delwath: You must know somebody, right?
Kenzo: That's what I was saying. Yeah, like, who is—give me, give me a couple names.
DM: Yeah, so my buddy, Andros.
Kenzo: Andros. Okay, is he in the—
DM: Oh, yeah, he's the one who rounds up muscle.
DM: I thought about joining up. They just seemed a bit zealous.
Kenzo: Are they kind of fanatical?
Kenzo: Like religious, fanatical, or just, anti-chalyte, fanatical?
DM: Kind of just fanatical, fanatical, although I heard the strangest thing yesterday from Andros.

DM: Kenzo. Strange visitor in the night.
DM: Or Delwath, strange visitor in my dreams.
Delwath: I came here to ask for your advice about Hektor.
Delwath: Have you heard any news out in the world of goings on in Chardon?
DM: That I had not heard. Hallelujah.
Delwath: All his works have fallen away. Those he corrupted are freed.
DM: This is a good day.
Delwath: We have Hektor here with us, trapped for the moment, but nobody knows him, and it's a bit disorienting coming out of a years long trance with nobody, you know, around.
Delwath: Didn't know if you had any advice, for I recalled you had spoken of him once from before his possession.
DM: Advice? I—I'm not sure, but he always liked music.
DM: He was a sailor, you know, before everything he was—
DM: He was not what you'd think, based on looks. He was shy and liked to sing, and to himself mostly, and listen to stories, not so much tell them.
DM: I met him a few times just when he was in port. You know we we were—must have been teenagers back then.
DM: I don't know what caught my eye about him, but I always felt bad.
DM: I mean he never talked much, but you know there was a sweetness to him. And he had a beautiful voice, never once heard him sing, since all the Fausto mess.
Delwath: How are you doing, by the way? Have you made it somewhere safe enough?
DM: Oh, it's not safe, not at all. But the dangers are ones I am proud to face.
Delwath: Things are changing in Chardon, I think.
DM: Oh, I'm done with Chardon. Up here in the Aurbez Plateau—
DM: Our dangers are more immediate.
DM: Strange monsters that come off the Plaguelands.

lines: Delwath: I just—I just kind of wanted to free Hektor, too, but we could—

Wellby: I think like for Hektor, like I I kind of like the idea of every day like Wellby calling him out, and like singing the the sailors shanties that he knew from the Green Sea, and like telling stories from his childhood on boats, and then slowly, like into that, starting to we—over a few days, like starting to weave bits and pieces of our adventures, and like almost telling the story of what's unfolded in the world over the last 15 years as a way to try to like anchor him back to his past, and also bring him into the present.
Delwath: Mean, we don't have to role play that out, indeed. But I like that. You know we can. We can put Wellby in charge of Hektor's rehabilitation.
